However, on the final lap, Blowfield started to pick up again and Steve Charlton and Tom Carter were also coming through the field to consolidate our scoring positions.

Our other men were well placed to begin with but as each lap came round, with the exception of Steve Charlton, they seemed to go further and further back while our most dangerous rivals, Sutton Harriers, had their men well up and going forward all the time.
Eddie Short ran the best of our men with Bill Lucas showing next best time and Steve Charlton and Tom Carter, despite a fall over a bicycle during his "leg," also ran well.

Archie Bedford won the 880 yards and also did this same distance in the medley relay to give us a winning lead in this event. Len Adams won the mile, beating Eddie Short and Steve Charlton. Jim Heathfield was second in the 440 and Terry Bateman won the high jump.
Bush ran well, in his usual dogged style, to gain second place, and Steve Charlton came through the field well to finish third.
Our first counter was Steve Charlton who finished 4th, and we were pleased to see Les. Stokell turning out for us once again, and he ran well in being 7th, as did C.
Jack Brown had come into third place and then Len Herbert just beat Stokell for fourth position. Steve Charlton had run his usual dogged race in being well up and a newcomer in J.

At the half-distance there was a group of four runners with Brown, Blowfield, Bill Lucas and Steve Charlton all nicely together in under the half-hour, which is good running for our five miles course.

Ted Stimpson ran his usual dependable race and Steve Charlton also did well as did Stan Davies, our new Track Captain, and with four in the first 33 we should have gained a place, but our fifth and sixth counters were too far back and so we had to be content with finishing fourth in the team race.
Les Stokell ran his usual determined kind of race while Jack Brown seemed content to take matters easy in front of Archie Bedford, Steve Charlton and Jack Bragginton.
Steve Charlton took over for the uphill stage through Redhill and on his first run in this race he did well in taking us up another two places and his time was the third fastest recorded on this leg.
Steve Charlton ran very well to finish 6th. Tom Carter and Stan Davies gave Steve good support and Bert Footer also qualified for a prize as the fourth member of our "A" team.
The 2 miles team race saw Bill Lucas lead the field home in 9 mins. 57 secs., and with good support from Reg Bolam (4th) and Steve Charlton (6th) we won the team race from Walton A.C.
In the 3 miles Team Race we had Jack Bragginton, George Lucas, Steve Charlton and Len Bishop, but could only manage a 4th place in this event.
In a 10 miles road race which started and finished on the track, our team of Steve Charlton, Tom Carter, Dick Towndrow and Roy Minahan came second in the team race which was won by the local club.
On the same day at Chertsey, Charlie Smart won an open 5 miles road race and with Steve Charlton fifth and Roy Minahan eighth, we beat Reading A.C. in the team race and so won another trophy.
P.S.—Had it not been for the unfortunate injury to Steve Charlton during the early part of the race, our forecast as above would have been almost realised.
First man home was John Bromley, of the Police, and he was closely followed by Bill Lucas, with Steve Charlton and Archie Bedford also well up.
Steve Charlton, who came into the team at the last moment owing to Len Herbert being indisposed, ran like a champion on the third stage and eventually handed over with a twenty-eight second lead.

In both events Belgrave were well to the fore, as in the senior event Ted Stimpson, Bill Lucas, Archie Bedford, Vern Blowfield, Eric Herbert, Jack Bragginton and Steve Charlton were well up, and Ray Tooby and Bob Taylor were in the lead in the junior race.
Steve Charlton once again finished as runner-up and seems to do better in the longer distance events where he is given a chance to settle down to some even-pace running.
Steve Charlton was another to do well and although at one time he had a bad attack of stitch, he kept going in his usual plucky fashion and did not yield any places.

We were unlucky in the fact that Steve Charlton injured his ankle soon after the start and was limping throughout the race. But for this I certainly think we should have been the first Southern club home and even so it was only the placing of our sixth man that decided this in favour of Aylesford Paper Mills.

Vern Blowfield showed a welcome return in finishing 12th with Len Adams 18th, Ken Stimpson 31st, Ted Stimpson 36th, Len Bishop 37th, Eric Bishop 40th, Doug Briggs 45th, Alan Bishop 48th, George Stace 49th, Steve Charlton 51st, Bob Taylor 52nd, A.
Vern Blowfield was 25th, Tony Snoad 26th, Bob Taylor 37th, Ken Stimpson 50th and Ted Stimpson 53rd. Others to finish were—Steve Charlton 54th, J.

Alan Sexton won the 220 yds. and Basil Walden won the 440, while Bob Belmore and Steve Charlton were 2nd and 3rd in the 1 mile match. We also won the 4 x 110 yds. relay and the final match points were—Belgrave H., 45; Essex Beagles, 25; Hercules A.C., 19.

It was not quite clear what happened to Steve Charlton who, after a very restrained start, put in a terrific burst and then retired hurt. In the team race Goodsell was well backed by Ken Honney who finished 4th and Addington, but the Flowers at 6th and 7th just gained the victory for Victoria Park.
Steve Charlton, showing much improved form, deservedly won the handicap. Second place in the handicap went to Clive Shippen who finished 5th in the actual race - a very good performance.
Good performances came from Steve Charlton, J.Moore and Alan Bishop, whilst new-comer R.Bhatia from Ceylon, astounded most of us by running well to the front and finishing in 8th position.

At Bexley we finished only one complete team out of three just because the following failed to write or phone me despite sufficient warning :- R.Linstead, S.Charlton, S.Boreham, G.Lines, D.Manning and R.Braine.
Ex-members, Geoff Goode and Steve Charlton were seen running for their new clubs. Semi-retired Bagnall would have been our third scoring man with his 56th place!!

We used to train on Tuesdays and Thursdays from Chelsea Barracks, tearing it up on the Hyde Park horse rides, plus the Saturday Inter-Club races, or training runs over the country; from those days I remember, Tom Carter, Bill Lucas, Bert Footer, Steve Charlton and many others".
Charlie went one better in the M60 5000m winning in 20:15.3, a good time in the hot conditions, although at M65 Steve Charlton flew round in an amazing 18:04.7 recording a new CBP.
Pat was less than half a minute behind the in form M65 winner Steve Charlton. Next was Charlie Walker, running a great deal better than he himself believed.

The Belgrave 10 mile Cross Country Championship at this time resulted in a win for Jack Brown in 59:31 from Steve Charlton and Bill Lucas.
